motto: Serving Greywater Falls since 1887, and the lake somewhat longer.
weather: Overcast, mild, 31°F, haze on the water nearly gone, that stovetop smell stronger by evening

undercurrent.phenomenon: an uncollected library card, due days ago, made out to nobody the town remembers; the pocket calendar's sixteen stamps run warm to the touch in a gradient, oldest warmest, and the drawer is now kept open rather than shut
undercurrent.note: Calloway's warmth gradient is the first physical, measurable escalation beyond handwriting comparison, which is why level jumps four points. Gerald touching the cover and answering unasked questions is the temptation-to-break-the-ritual paying off exactly as planned, but gently, not as a full relapse into writing. Doreen's vanished fourth-chair loaf is a new small wrongness seeded for tomorrow, ideally tied back to the alcove's ninth-book origin. Agnes remains held in reserve; her last riddle should land within the next few days, possibly in writing, possibly timed to when the level crosses into stage 3 territory. Keep Russ's file-closing sturdy but let one crack show soon, maybe about the open drawer specifically since it violates his 'system worked as designed' logic.

editor.name: Wren Aldercott
editor.voice: Dry, precise, allergic to drama, which is unfortunate given recent events. Writes like a person holding a clipboard while standing in rising water. Lets one true thing slip per edition, usually in the last line.

season_arc.premise: Calloway finishes reshelving the east alcove in the last cataloguer's 2009 order and finds, tucked behind where the ninth book sat, a library card checked out that same interrupted Wednesday and never returned. It is due back today. The borrower's name is nobody currently living in Greywater Falls has ever heard of, and the little pocket calendar stamped inside has fourteen years of due-date stamps on it already, one for every year since, each in a different hand.
